Jobvite pricing starts at roughly $400 per month for small teams and scales to $5,000+ per month for enterprise organizations, based on third-party estimates through 2026. No prices are published publicly. Every deal requires a custom quote based on your hiring volume, recruiter seat count, and selected modules.

As part of [Employ Inc.](https://www.employinc.com/) alongside Lever and JazzHR, Jobvite sits within a three-platform portfolio that segments by company size. JazzHR handles SMBs. Lever covers mid-market. Upper mid-market and enterprise are Jobvite's natural fit. Companies considered too small for the platform usually get redirected to JazzHR or Lever - often at a lower price point but with fewer features.

This guide breaks down Jobvite's estimated costs, maps out the add-on fees that surface after the initial quote, explains the recruiting limitations most reviews skip over, and compares Jobvite to five ATS alternatives. Whether you're evaluating Jobvite for the first time or approaching a renewal, you'll know what to budget for (see also our best recruiting software guide). If you're also comparing platforms, our [Greenhouse](https://www.pin.com/blog/greenhouse-pricing/), [iCIMS](https://www.pin.com/blog/icims-pricing/), and [SmartRecruiters](https://www.pin.com/blog/smartrecruiters-pricing/) pricing breakdowns cover those in the same detail.

> **TL;DR:**
>
> - **Quotes range widely with no public pricing.** Estimates run from $4,800/yr for sub-100 employee teams to $60,000+/yr for 1,000+ employees ([SoftwareFinder](https://softwarefinder.com/resources/jobvite-cost-pricing), [eLearning Industry](https://elearningindustry.com/jobvite-pricing-plans-and-costs-everything-you-need-to-know), 2025).
> - **Implementation adds $1,000-$10,000.** Setup, data migration, and integration fees are separate from annual license costs.
> - **Module add-ons inflate the base quote.** CRM, onboarding, recruitment marketing, video interviews, and AI each sit in separate modules with their own fees.
> - **Best for mid-market and enterprise.** Jobvite targets 250+ employee organizations; Employ Inc. steers smaller teams toward JazzHR or Lever in the same portfolio.
> - **Pin is a complement, not a replacement.** Jobvite is an ATS, not a sourcing engine. [Pin](https://www.pin.com/) starts at $99/mo with a free tier for teams that need proactive candidate outreach.

## What Does Jobvite Actually Cost in 2026?

According to [SoftwareFinder](https://softwarefinder.com/resources/jobvite-cost-pricing) (2025) and [eLearning Industry](https://elearningindustry.com/jobvite-pricing-plans-and-costs-everything-you-need-to-know) (2025), Jobvite's per-employee-per-month cost falls roughly between $7 and $11 PEPM. But those are estimates from third-party aggregators, not confirmed by Jobvite. Pricing lives entirely behind a sales wall.

Here's what companies are estimated to pay based on available data:

<figure style="margin:2rem 0;padding:0;line-height:0"><img src="data:image/svg+xml;base64," alt="Estimated Jobvite Annual Cost by Company Size" style="width:100%;height:auto;display:block;border-radius:12px"></figure>

Keep in mind these are rough estimates, not verified contract data. Your actual Jobvite cost depends on hiring volume, selected modules, and how hard you negotiate. Two companies with identical headcounts can pay very different amounts.

Even so, a few patterns are worth noting about the pricing model:

-   **No public pricing at all.** Unlike Workable (which publishes its rates), Jobvite requires a sales demo before you see any numbers. That means you can't compare costs without investing time in a discovery call.
-   **Per-employee scaling.** Your bill grows with headcount, even if your recruiting team stays the same size. A 500-person company on Jobvite might pay 7-10x more than a 50-person company for the same core features.
-   **Module-based pricing.** The base ATS is one price. CRM, onboarding, recruitment marketing, video interviews, and AI features are add-on modules with separate costs. The base quote rarely reflects what you'll actually spend.
-   **Annual contracts standard.** Jobvite typically sells annual agreements. Month-to-month billing isn't publicly offered.

One wrinkle most pricing guides miss: the Employ Inc. portfolio dynamic. Companies with under 250 employees often get redirected to Lever or JazzHR by the sales team - not necessarily a bad outcome, since they'd pay less for a platform sized to their needs. Even so, it means the real floor price is higher than estimates suggest, because the smallest companies never actually get a Jobvite quote.

Talking to our customers, the Jobvite evaluation story follows a predictable pattern. Teams of 300-500 employees shortlist Jobvite alongside Greenhouse and Lever. They pick Jobvite for its recruitment marketing suite and CRM breadth. Six months in, they add Pin to handle sourcing because the ATS doesn't find candidates proactively. Pairing ATS with Pin costs less than a single enterprise platform that claims to do both. From our conversations with recruiting teams that made this switch: Jobvite manages the pipeline, and Pin fills it. That framing doesn't appear in most Jobvite pricing reviews, but it's the approach recruiting teams consistently land on after trying to stretch an ATS into a sourcing tool.

## What Features Does Jobvite Include?

Four core areas define the Jobvite recruiting CRM platform: ATS, CRM, recruitment marketing, and onboarding. Employ Inc. has been investing heavily in AI-powered features across its portfolio since mid-2025, announcing 30+ innovations at its [June 2025 AI Companion launch](https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2025/06/03/3092710/0/en/Employ-Unveils-Bold-AI-Companion-Strategy-Responsible-AI-Built-for-Recruiters-Designed-for-Impact.html). Among those: an AI Interview Companion for automated intake summaries and an AI Screening Companion with IBM watsonx-powered bias monitoring.

Here's what the platform includes and what costs extra:

| Feature | Included in Base | Add-On |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Applicant Tracking (Evolve ATS) | ✅ |  |
| Resume Parsing & Boolean Search | ✅ |  |

| Employee Referrals Module |  | 💰 Separate module |

In practice, the base platform is genuinely full-featured for applicant tracking and CRM. More is bundled into the core than at most competitors - career site builder, recruitment marketing, and CRM are typically add-ons at platforms like Greenhouse or iCIMS. That said, the newer AI features and onboarding tools are separate purchases, and the vendor doesn't disclose their individual pricing.

### The AI Companion Strategy

Rolled out across all three Employ platforms in 2025, these AI Companions each target a different workflow stage. Intake summaries, AI-guided interview kits, and instant ATS feedback are what the Interview Companion handles. Launched in November 2025, the Screening Companion handles candidate matching and engagement monitoring. As of May 2026, it includes built-in bias monitoring via IBM watsonx.governance - a notable differentiator for companies in regulated industries.

An AI Sourcing Companion is reportedly still in development and wasn't available as of late 2025. That gap matters. CRM tools handle nurture campaigns for candidates already in your system, but none of that searches external databases to find new candidates. For teams where sourcing is the bottleneck, a separate tool becomes necessary regardless of modules purchased.

## What Hidden Fees Does Jobvite Charge?

Beyond the base subscription, three cost categories inflate Jobvite's true price. These are: a one-time implementation fee of $1,000-$10,000, undisclosed annual fees for each add-on module, and integration charges that can reach five figures for specific connectors. At $17.22 billion in 2025 and projected to reach $18.57 billion in 2026, the ATS market keeps expanding, per [Fortune Business Insights](https://www.fortunebusinessinsights.com/applicant-tracking-system-market-108826) (2025). As the market grows, vendor pricing complexity grows with it. Jobvite's base subscription is only part of the picture.

### 1\. Implementation and Onboarding Fees

One-time implementation runs $1,000 for small deployments up to $10,000 for enterprise rollouts, based on [eLearning Industry](https://elearningindustry.com/jobvite-pricing-plans-and-costs-everything-you-need-to-know) (2025) estimates. Implementation covers data migration from your existing ATS, workflow configuration, integration setup, and initial training. Expect 4-8 weeks for a standard deployment.

### 2\. Integration Fees

With 300+ advertised integrations - ADP, Workday, Oracle, and LinkedIn Apply Connect among them - most work out of the box. But reviewers on [Capterra](https://www.capterra.com/p/109268/Jobvite/reviews/) report that some integrations require additional fees - one reviewer cited a $50,000 charge for a specific integration to function. Ask for a complete integration cost breakdown during your sales process, not after signing.

### 3\. Module Add-Ons

Onboarding, video interviews, employee referrals, and each AI Companion feature are sold as separate modules. None of these prices are disclosed publicly. A company that starts with just the base ATS and CRM might add onboarding, AI Interview Companion, and referrals over time - each at an undisclosed annual cost. The total cost can creep significantly above the initial quote.

### 4\. Annual Renewal Increases

Like most enterprise ATS platforms, Jobvite's contracts typically include annual price escalators. The exact percentage varies by contract, but 5-10% annual increases are common in the ATS category. Lock in your renewal rate during initial negotiations if possible. If your Year 1 cost is $20,000, budget for $22,000-$24,000 by Year 3 before adding any new modules.

Worth examining separately: the integration fee structure. That list of 300+ integrations looks impressive on the marketing page, but the gap between "we integrate with X" and "that integration works at no extra cost" can reach five figures. Before signing, request a written confirmation that every integration you need is included in your quoted price.

## What Are Jobvite's Biggest Limitations?

Weak reporting, inconsistent support, and no external candidate sourcing are Jobvite's three most common complaints, recurring across its 4.0/5 rating on [G2](https://www.g2.com/products/jobvite/reviews) (480+ reviews) and 4.1/5 on [Capterra](https://www.capterra.com/p/109268/Jobvite/reviews/) (566 reviews). Much of the platform performs well, but these patterns emerge consistently in the negative reviews.

**Reporting is weak.** This is the most frequent complaint across review platforms. Users describe the reporting suite as limited, unintuitive, and difficult to customize. One [TrustRadius](https://www.trustradius.com/products/jobvite/reviews) reviewer noted: "Reporting is awful. They updated their reporting structure and it is not the most efficient." For teams that need custom recruiting analytics, this is a real gap.

**Customer support is inconsistent.** Multiple reviewers describe slow response times and support agents who lack deep product knowledge. TrustRadius users specifically flag the live chat as "almost useless." Enterprise customers with premium support contracts report better experiences, but standard support lags.

**No external candidate sourcing.** Jobvite's CRM manages candidates who are already in your system. It doesn't search external databases to find new candidates. There's no equivalent to searching 850M+ profiles, identifying passive candidates, or running AI-matched sourcing queries. If your recruiting team's bottleneck is finding candidates rather than managing applicants, this is a fundamental gap.

**Overkill for small teams.** Capterra reviewers with under 100 employees frequently describe the platform as too complex and too expensive for their needs. Jobvite's sales team often redirects these prospects to JazzHR or Lever, which confirms the platform's positioning as a mid-market and enterprise tool.

**Slow development pace (historically).** Before the 2025 AI Companion rollout, multiple G2 reviewers described Jobvite's feature development as slow relative to competitors. The AI investments have accelerated the roadmap, but it's worth asking about planned feature releases during your evaluation.

Solid scores for a recruiting platform with a 15-year enterprise track record - though the aggregate rating masks a clear split between teams who find it fits their workflow and those who find it overkill.

Reviewers who rate the Jobvite ATS highly are typically at enterprise companies (500+ employees) with dedicated TA teams who need ATS, CRM, and recruitment marketing in one platform. The Jobvite recruiting software experience is strongest when your bottleneck is managing applicants, not finding them.

In summary: Workable is the only platform with publicly listed pricing ($299-$719/mo). Jobvite, Greenhouse, Lever, SmartRecruiters, and iCIMS all require custom quotes, with mid-market estimates ranging from ~$15,000/yr (Lever) to $20,781/yr (iCIMS). Pin's published $99/mo with a free tier makes it the most accessible starting point for sourcing alongside any ATS.

A few patterns stand out:

**Workable is the only ATS with fully public pricing** in this set. When pricing transparency matters to your procurement process, that's a significant differentiator. Every other platform on this list requires a sales conversation. See [Workable pricing 2026](https://www.pin.com/blog/workable-pricing/) for our full breakdown.

**Lever is Jobvite's closest competitor** - and it's owned by the same company. Lever's CRM capabilities are widely considered stronger than Jobvite's, with a cleaner UI and better nurture workflows. Lever's analytics and reporting are thinner, though, and it lacks Jobvite's built-in recruitment marketing tools. Choosing between the two comes down to whether CRM depth (Lever) or feature breadth (Jobvite) matters more. Many mid-market teams end up on Lever simply because the price point is lower.

**iCIMS commands the highest price point** in this comparison. Average contracts run $20,781/yr, per [People Managing People](https://peoplemanagingpeople.com/tools/icims-pricing/) (2025). Its integration library and analytics are broad, but implementation typically runs 3-6 months for enterprise deployments. Teams with 1,000+ employees and complex multi-region workflows can justify the premium; for everyone else, Jobvite or Greenhouse at 30-40% lower cost is hard to argue against. Our [iCIMS pricing breakdown](https://www.pin.com/blog/icims-pricing/) covers the full cost picture.

**None of these ATS platforms do proactive sourcing.** All six manage candidates after they've entered your pipeline. Searching external databases, running automated outreach campaigns, or matching candidates using AI sourcing - none of that is included in any of these systems. Where finding candidates is the bottleneck, a dedicated sourcing tool is necessary alongside whichever ATS you choose. See our guide to the [ATS buyer's guide for 2026](https://www.pin.com/blog/best-applicant-tracking-systems/) for a full comparison.

## Who Should Buy Jobvite?

Data from Employ Inc.'s [2026 benchmarks report](https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2026/01/07/3214475/0/en/What-Will-Good-Hiring-Look-Like-in-2026-New-Employ-Inc-Report-Reveals-Key-Recruiting-Benchmarks.html) covers 6,640 customers across Jobvite, Lever, and JazzHR. Across those platforms, time to fill dropped from 67.7 days in 2024 to 63.5 days in 2025, and first-year turnover fell from 23.7% to 12.1%. Real improvements - though the figures span all three Employ products, not Jobvite alone.

A strong fit when:

-   Your company has 250+ employees with a dedicated TA team
-   You need ATS, CRM, and recruitment marketing in a single platform (not bolted together from separate tools)
-   Your hiring is primarily inbound - managing applicants, nurturing talent pools, and running career site campaigns
-   You want 300+ integrations with major HRIS and payroll systems (ADP, Workday, Oracle)
-   You're in a regulated industry where IBM watsonx-powered bias monitoring matters

A poor fit when:

-   You have fewer than 250 employees. Jobvite's own sales team will likely redirect you to JazzHR or Lever.
-   Your bottleneck is finding candidates, not managing them. External sourcing is not included.
-   You need transparent, self-serve pricing. Every quote requires a sales conversation.
-   Custom reporting is critical to your workflow. Reviewers consistently flag this as a weakness.
-   You're on a tight budget. At $18,000+/yr estimated for mid-market, add-ons push the true cost higher.

One common mistake is buying Jobvite expecting it to handle sourcing. Once candidates are in the pipeline, Jobvite manages them well - but it won't find them for you. Recruiting teams that need both applicant management and proactive sourcing typically run an ATS alongside a dedicated AI sourcing tool - and the combined cost is often comparable to a single enterprise platform.

## Frequently Asked Questions

### How much does Jobvite cost per year?

Annual costs run approximately $4,800/yr for small teams and $60,000+/yr for enterprise organizations, based on third-party estimates from [SoftwareFinder](https://softwarefinder.com/resources/jobvite-cost-pricing) (2025). Per-employee-per-month rates fall roughly between $7 and $11. Implementation adds $1,000-$10,000 one-time. No pricing is published publicly - every quote requires a sales call.

### Is Jobvite worth it for small businesses?

Probably not. Jobvite is designed for mid-market and enterprise teams with 250+ employees and dedicated recruiting staff. Companies under 100 employees frequently describe the platform as overly complex and expensive on [Capterra](https://www.capterra.com/p/109268/Jobvite/reviews/) and [G2](https://www.g2.com/products/jobvite/reviews). Employ Inc. typically steers smaller companies toward JazzHR or Lever instead.

### What's the difference between Jobvite and Lever?

Both are owned by Employ Inc. but target different segments. Lever focuses on mid-market teams with strong CRM and nurture capabilities. Jobvite targets upper mid-market and enterprise with broader feature coverage including recruitment marketing and deeper analytics. Lever is generally less expensive, with estimated costs starting at $3,500/yr versus Jobvite's $4,800/yr.

### Does Jobvite do candidate sourcing?

No. Jobvite's CRM manages candidates already in your system through nurture campaigns and relationship tracking. It doesn't search external databases to find new candidates, run automated outreach to passive talent, or offer AI-powered candidate matching from external profiles. For proactive sourcing, teams pair Jobvite with dedicated tools like Pin, which searches 850M+ profiles.

### What are the benefits of using Jobvite?

Jobvite's core strengths are its bundled ATS-CRM-recruitment marketing suite, 300+ integrations with major HRIS platforms (ADP, Workday, Oracle), and a career site builder included in the base subscription rather than as an add-on. For mid-market and enterprise companies doing primarily inbound hiring, the platform manages the full pipeline from job posting through onboarding. Since 2025, the AI Companions (Interview and Screening) add automated intake summaries and IBM watsonx-powered bias monitoring - a meaningful differentiator for regulated industries.

### What ATS platform has the most transparent pricing?

Workable is the only major ATS that publishes full pricing on its website: $299/mo (Standard) to $719/mo (Enterprise). Greenhouse, iCIMS, SmartRecruiters, Lever, and Jobvite all require custom quotes. If pricing transparency impacts your buying decision, Workable and dedicated sourcing tools like Pin ($99/mo, published pricing with free tier) stand apart from the field.

## The Bottom Line on Jobvite Pricing

Capable as an enterprise ATS-CRM, Jobvite has genuine strengths in recruitment marketing, analytics, and AI-powered interview tools. Its position within the Employ Inc. portfolio means you're buying from a company with 23,000+ customers across three complementary products. Since 2025, the AI Companions (Interview and Screening) have strengthened the roadmap in ways most reviews underweight.

Understanding Jobvite pricing in full requires committing to a sales process. Estimated costs of $18,000+/yr for mid-market companies put it in line with Greenhouse and above Lever. Add-on modules, implementation fees, and annual escalators push the total cost higher than the initial quote suggests.

For teams whose primary challenge is managing applicants and nurturing talent pools, Jobvite delivers. For teams whose primary challenge is finding candidates in the first place, the investment is better directed toward tools built for that purpose.
